risks: No participants and no personal data; the risk is misuse of the result, for example presenting a prescribing gain as fewer strokes or pressuring people who declined treatment.
consent: Not applicable: published reviews only. Any later local intervention that uses the gap register will need its own consent and governance review.
data: Published data only; extraction sheets and the citation matrix are shared openly with the report.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: extract age, sex, care home residence, dementia, deprivation and ethnicity of included populations, and report where people on the register (for example care home residents and people with dementia) are missing from the evidence. Treat an informed decline as a legitimate outcome, not a failure.
effectiveness: The overview tells the board which intervention types have evidence of raising appropriate anticoagulation and how certain that is.
efficiency: Uses existing library support and four analyst hours a week; avoids funding an intervention without evidence.
grants: None needed; the result may support a funded local evaluation of the chosen intervention.
partnerships: Health board library, the prevention committee, two patient partners with atrial fibrillation (one who declined anticoagulation) and a general practitioner adviser.
rebPath: No research ethics review is needed for a review of published literature; the protocol is registered publicly before screening, which is the gate the accepted decision is waiting for.
limitations: Depends on the quality and overlap of existing reviews; recent primary studies not yet in a review are missed.
summary: No participants; the ethical risks are misreading the result and pressuring people who declined treatment.
